headline: Is AI development becoming the new gambling?
summary: Developers are reportedly spending increasing amounts on AI tools, with some losing track of time and money in a cycle of prompts and near-misses.
details: The use of AI tools for software development is drawing comparisons to gambling, with developers exhibiting similar behavioral patterns.
The initial promise of AI was to save time, but some users are reportedly spending more time and money on AI subscriptions, chasing productivity gains.
Users are described as making 'microbets' on every prompt, experiencing a rush when the AI delivers correct results, similar to the dopamine hit from winning a bet.
Frustration from AI failures and the 'near-miss effect' of close calls reportedly encourage users to continue prompting, potentially lowering judgment and scrutiny.
This behavior raises concerns about whether developers are taking more risks and producing code with less oversight due to the addictive nature of AI interactions.

headline_marked: Apple unveils [[iPhone Duo]] with variable aperture camera
headline: Apple unveils iPhone Duo with variable aperture camera
summary: Apple's CEO John Ternus makes his debut with the new iPhone Duo and iPhone 18 Pro, featuring an innovative variable aperture camera and new AI features for Apple Watch.
details: Apple has officially launched its first foldable smartphone, the iPhone Duo, aiming to compete in the growing foldable market. The device, showcased by CEO John Ternus in his first major product unveiling, appears to incorporate design elements from existing Android foldables.

The iPhone 18 Pro also received an update, featuring a new variable aperture camera. While Apple highlights the ability to stop down the aperture, reviewers are questioning whether this offers a significant upgrade over a wider aperture alone.

New Apple Watches were also introduced, boasting an updated sensor array. The company claims these sensors enable new health metrics, though there's discussion on whether they provide genuinely new data or simply more 'vibes-based' health information.

A notable addition to the Apple Watch is an always-on microphone capable of summarizing conversations, raising questions about privacy and data usage. The Vergecast discussed these new AI features and their implications.
Beyond the hardware, the episode also touched upon the state of running local Large Language Models (LLMs) on Mac devices, featuring a segment with AI researcher CJ Trowbridge.
caption:
Apple's first foldable, the iPhone Duo, is here. Plus, a variable aperture camera on the iPhone 18 Pro and new AI features for Apple Watch.

Apple has officially launched its first foldable smartphone, the iPhone Duo, aiming to compete in the growing foldable market. The device, showcased by CEO John Ternus in his first major product unveiling, appears to incorporate design elements from existing Android foldables.

The iPhone 18 Pro also received an update, featuring a new variable aperture camera. While Apple highlights the ability to stop down the aperture, reviewers are questioning whether this offers a significant upgrade over a wider aperture alone.

New Apple Watches were also introduced, boasting an updated sensor array. The company claims these sensors enable new health metrics, though there's discussion on whether they provide genuinely new data or simply more 'vibes-based' health information.

A notable addition to the Apple Watch is an always-on microphone capable of summarizing conversations, raising questions about privacy and data usage. The Vergecast discussed these new AI features and their implications.

Beyond the hardware, the episode also touched upon the state of running local Large Language Models (LLMs) on Mac devices, featuring a segment with AI researcher CJ Trowbridge.
